title: GPU OOM debugging notes - Ethan Park
notes:
Goal: quick breadcrumbs for GPU OOM / CUDA driver/library mismatch issues I hit while onboarding a new LLM worker image. Personal scratchpad - rough, partial hypotheses, commands I ran and outputs I cared about, and what fixed (or didn't).

Summary of the incident:
- Symptom: frequent RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory during inference boot (first few batches) on gpu-node-03. Same model sometimes works on other nodes.
- Also saw occasional: 'CUDA driver version is insufficient for CUDA runtime' and 'libcublas.so.10: cannot open shared object file' in container logs when switching to a different image.

Commands and outputs I ran (raw-ish):
1) nvidia-smi (on host)
$ nvidia-smi
Thu Nov  2 09:14:02 2024
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| NVIDIA-SMI 535.86.10    Driver Version: 535.86.10    CUDA Version: 12.1     |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| GPU  Name        Persistence-M| Bus-Id        Disp.A | Volatile Uncorr. ECC |
| 0    A100-SXM4-40G      Off   | 00000000:3B:00.0 Off |                  N/A |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+

2) inside container: python quick check
>>> import torch
>>> torch.cuda.is_available()
True
>>> torch.version.cuda
'11.8'
>>> torch.cuda.get_device_properties(0)
<...shows 40GB mem...>

Note: host driver CUDA 12.1, container PyTorch built against CUDA 11.8. This is normally fine (driver >= runtime), but other libraries can mismatch (cuBLAS/cuDNN).

3) error snapshot (stack trace excerpt)
RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 9.00 GiB (GPU 0; 39.34 GiB total capacity; 32.47 GiB already allocated; 1.24 GiB free; 33.12 GiB reserved in total by PyTorch)
  File "/opt/model/serve.py", line 142, in handle_request
    out = model.generate(inputs, max_new_tokens=512, do_sample=False)

Observations: 'already allocated' is high immediately at startup. Suspect warmup or persistent cache from previous process inside same container, or pinned memory leakage across threads.

Commands to inspect processes and memory on GPU:
$ nvidia-smi pmon -c 1
# shows PID 22415 (python) using 32GB
$ ps aux | grep 22415
root   22415  0.3  2.1  214324 832144 ? Sl   09:12   0:12 python -u serve.py

Hypotheses:
- H1: Model warmup / KV cache allocation happens before we clear anything; batch size too high.
- H2: A stray process from previous run didn't exit cleanly and retained memory.
- H3: Mixed CUDA/CUDNN/cuBLAS versions in container vs host cause degraded allocation behavior (fallbacks, pinned memory).
- H4: Using torch.compile or custom kernels that allocate large workspaces (cublasLt) with mismatch leads to large initial reservation.

Quick mitigations tried (results inline):
- Lowered batch size from 8 -> 2: reduced peak usage, inference succeeds for single requests. Partial fix.
- torch.cuda.empty_cache() after model loading: reduced reserved by a couple GB but not to desired baseline.
- export TORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:128 - small impact.
- model.half() (fp16) + with torch.no_grad(): big reduction, but introduced numerical issues for some prompts.
- enable gradient_checkpointing (for model init): only applies to training, not inference.
- Restart node (reboot): cleared stuck processes; subsequent runs still had high reservation but stable.

More severe library mismatches observed later when trying a community image:
- Container A: PyTorch built with CUDA 11.8 and cuDNN 8.2. Host driver supports CUDA 12.1. Works in many cases.
- Container B: custom image had references to /usr/local/cuda-11.0 and explicit LD_LIBRARY_PATH pointing to old libs. Error on startup:
	libcublas.so.10: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory
	or
	Failed to load libcudnn.so.7 - wrong version

Diagnosis pattern for driver/runtime lib mismatches:
- If driver < required by runtime -> immediate 'CUDA driver version is insufficient for CUDA runtime'.
- If container points to wrong cuBLAS/cuDNN libs -> 'cannot open shared object file' or unpredictable fallback slowdowns and larger allocations.

Commands to inspect library linking inside container:
$ ldconfig -p | grep libcudnn
	libcudnn.so.8 (libc6,x86-64) => /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcudnn.so.8
$ ls -l /usr/local/cuda*/lib64 | head
	lrwxrwxrwx 1 root root 14 Sep 28  2023 /usr/local/cuda -> /usr/local/cuda-11.8
	-rw-r--r-- 1 root root  12 Nov  1  2023 /usr/local/cuda/version.txt
$ cat /usr/local/cuda/version.txt	CUDA Version 11.8.89

What I tried to align libs:
- Removed LD_LIBRARY_PATH overrides so container picks host /usr/lib libs. Fixed a mismatch where container was using ancient cuBLAS.
- pip uninstall torch; pip install "torch==2.2.0+cu118" - tried to match cu118 but some other deps wanted different cudatoolkit. This reduced some runtime warnings.
- On one node re-installed driver 535.x (already present) and ensured host libs symlinked to /usr/local/cuda -> points to 12.x on some nodes, 11.8 on others. We standardized to 12.1 on nodes where everything else is updated.

Edge case: PyTorch built with different CUDA version reports torch.version.cuda='11.8' even if host driver is 12.1. That's normal. The key problem is when custom compiled extensions (apex, triton, fused kernels) are linked against older libcudnn/cuBLAS.

Useful diagnostics to collect per incident (scriptable):
- nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,name,memory.total,memory.free,driver_version --format=csv
- ps aux | grep -E 'python|triton|fused' and map PIDs to GPU usage (nvidia-smi pmon / nvidia-smi -i 0 --query-compute-apps=pid,process_name,used_memory --format=csv)
- inside container: ldconfig -p | grep -i cuda && readlink -f /usr/local/cuda && cat /usr/local/cuda/version.txt
- pip freeze | grep torch && python -c "import torch;print(torch.version.cuda, torch.backends.cudnn.version())"
- check for stale /dev/shm usage, tmp files used by kernels (rare but seen).

Longer term mitigations and notes for runbooks:
- Enforce base images that don't override /usr/lib CUDA libs; rely on driver >= runtime rule. Avoid shipping older cuBLAS/cuDNN in images unless pinned and tested.
- Add startup sanity checks in our container entrypoint: compare host driver (nvidia-smi driver) vs torch.version.cuda and warn if common mismatch patterns present; fail fast for known-incompatible combos.
- Instrument early memory footprint: log torch.cuda.memory_reserved(0), allocated, max_reserved at service start and after model load to detect unusually-large reservations.
- Auto-reduce batch size on OOM and return 429 with hint to client. Better than retries that thrash GPU.
- For inference image variants, provide an fp16/amp mode and a safe-fp32 fallback. Make fp16 opt-in via config.
- For fused kernels / triton artifacts, pin exact build matrix per image and include a test harness that runs small allocs and validates expected memory behavior.

Notes on a weird case: 'Illegal instruction (core dumped)' on node-05 while loading a triton op. Root cause: triton wheel built on newer glibc/AVX512 not compatible with node CPU microcode. Fix: rebuild triton on compatible baseline or use CPU feature targeting. Not directly OOM but manifests during model init so looks like OOM.

What eventually helped for this run:
- Rebuilt container removing legacy LD_LIBRARY_PATH overrides + installed torch wheel matching cu118 (consistent with most libraries) -> stable runs.
- Added entrypoint memory logging and auto-batch size throttle to reduce initial peak.

Open follow-ups/ToDos (actionable):
- [ ] Add container startup check script to repo (quick script that prints driver, torch.version.cuda, libcudnn version). (Owner: me)
- [ ] Add post-deploy smoke test that runs small generate to validate allocation profile. (Owner: eng-sre)
- [ ] Investigate using unified image baseline (cu12) across nodes; evaluate GPU drivers and compatibility with existing wheels. (Owner: infra)

Slack breadcrumbs: see channel #gpu-debug-threads, message ts 1642 for repro commands and a small core dump attached.

If I come back to this later, check: did we ever see a reproducible memory leak tied to our token cache across requests? I suspect some of the high 'already allocated' numbers came from persistent processes started by k8s probe (old executor) that weren't cleaned up.

Endnotes: this doc is a working scratchpad. I'll split the stable checks into a small script and shove into infra/containers repo once validated.
